title: Backtracking: Generate Parentheses
oneLiner: Every balanced string of n pairs of parentheses. Build left to right, adding ( while you have some left and ) only while it would close an open one.
keyTakeaway: Never build an invalid prefix and you never need to check validity at the end. Track open and close counts: you may add ( if open < n, and ) if close < open. When the string reaches length 2n it is balanced by construction. The count of results is the n-th Catalan number.
explanation:
Return all strings of n pairs of parentheses that are balanced (every ) closes an earlier (). For n = 3 there are five: ((())), (()()), (())(), ()(()), ()()(). The grader sorts your list, so any order is fine.

Brute force would generate all 2^(2n) strings of ( and ) and keep the valid ones, checking each with a counter like Valid Parentheses. Backtracking does better by refusing to grow a prefix that can't become valid. A prefix can still be completed exactly when it never closes more than it has opened and never opens more than n.

So recurse on (current string, open, close). If the length is 2n, record it. Otherwise two choices, each with its own guard: if open < n, try adding "("; if close < open, try adding ")". The second guard is the key one, since it means there is an unmatched ( to close. Strings are immutable, so passing current + "(" down the recursion needs no explicit undo; with a StringBuilder or list you would append, recurse and remove.

Every leaf of this search tree is a valid answer, so the work is proportional to the output. The number of balanced strings is the n-th Catalan number, about 4^n / (n^1.5 · √π), and each has length 2n. The recursion is only 2n deep.

The visualization runs n = 2.

def generate_parenthesis(n):

        # If close_count < open_count, build(current + ")", open_count, close_count + 1).
        pass

    build("", 0, 0)
    return result

recognitionSignals: Generate all valid strings or structures where validity is a running count (balance, depth, budget).
A constraint you can check on each prefix: prune as you build instead of filtering at the end.
gotchas: Guarding ) with close < n instead of close < open produces strings like ())(.
Stopping at length n instead of 2n.
With a shared StringBuilder, forgetting to remove the last character after the recursive call.
confusableWith: Valid Parentheses checks one given string with a stack; here you generate all of them, and a counter replaces the stack because there is only one bracket type.
Subsets and Combination Sum choose from a list of items; here the two choices are always ( and ), and the guards do the pruning.

complexity.note: The number of answers is the n-th Catalan number, roughly 4ⁿ / n^1.5, and each costs O(n) to build, so the time is exponential (bounded by the 2^(2n) prefixes of length 2n). The recursion is 2n deep, O(n), not counting the output.
